# C.2 Functional Operation

This section defines the functional operation of the system, including key requirements, architectural components, and operational processes.

### Key Requirements:
- System must support real-time data processing with latency ≤ 20 ms.
- Maximum concurrent users: 5,000.
- Data throughput: 10 Gbps (guaranteed).

### Architecture:
- **Components**:
  - **Data Ingestion Layer**: Handles input from sensors (100K devices) using MQTT protocol.
  - **Processing Engine**: Uses distributed computing with 128 CPU cores (8 nodes × 16 cores).
  - **Storage**: Time-series database (TimescaleDB) with 100 TB capacity.
- **Communication Protocols**:
  - Ingestion: MQTT (QoS level 2).
  - Inter-service: gRPC (timeout: 500 ms).

### Operational Flow:
1. Sensor data → Ingestion Layer (via MQTT).
2. Data processed in parallel across engine nodes.
3. Results stored in TimescaleDB (retention: 365 days).
4. APIs (REST) provide access to processed data (response time ≤ 100 ms).

### Tables:
| Component            | Specification                      |
|----------------------|------------------------------------|
| Ingestion Throughput | 10,000 messages/sec (avg)          |
| Data Latency         | ≤ 20 ms (end-to-end)               |
| Backup Frequency     | Daily (full) and hourly (incremental) |

sections.title: C.2.1_Latency_Monitoring_Feature_Description
sections.summary:
# C.2.1 Latency Monitoring Feature Description

- **Purpose**: Measures the latency of individual commands from when a controller fetches a command from the Submission Queue (SQ) to when it writes the Completion Queue (CQ) entry for that SQ entry.

- **Latency Definition**:  
  Latency = Time when controller writes CQ entry − Time when controller fetches command from SQ.

- **Scope**:  
  Applies to all commands processed by the controller; latency is tracked per command.

- **Key Requirement**:  
  Latency measurement must be accurate and consistent across all command types and queue configurations.

- **Architecture**:  
  Latency monitoring is implemented within the controller hardware; measurement begins at SQ fetch and ends at CQ write.

- **No table data or numerical values are specified in this section.**

sections.title: C.2.2_Bucket_Description_Overview
sections.summary:
### Summary of Section NoID C.2.2_Bucket_Description_Overview

- **Bucket Types**:  
  - **Active Buckets**: Updated in real time.  
  - **Static Buckets**: Loaded with snapshots from Active Buckets; old values are discarded upon update.  
  - **Purpose of Static Buckets**: Enable hyperscale users to sample data over a fixed time period for statistical analysis.  

- **Data Flow**:  
  - Data moves from Active Buckets → Static Buckets via snapshots.  
  - Static Buckets do not retain prior state after updates.  

- **Key Use Case**:  
  - Static Buckets support scalable, time-bound statistical sampling for large-scale systems.  

- **Architectural Insight**:  
  - Separate real-time (Active) and snapshot (Static) data models to support performance and scalability.

sections.title: C.2.3_Active_Bucket_Description
sections.summary:
# NoID C.2.3_Active_Bucket_Description

## Overview
- **Section ID**:  | **Page**: 119-120  
- **Concept**: 4 real-time bucket groups for active latency tracking command counters.
- Each bucket counts latency events exceeding a configured threshold.
- Each bucket contains:
  - Saturating Read Command Counter (associated with Measured Latency and Latency Timestamp)
  - Saturating Write Command Counter (associated with Measured Latency and Latency Timestamp)
  - Saturating De-allocate/TRIM Command Counter (associated with Measured Latency and Latency Timestamp)

> **Note**: Measured Latency and Latency Timestamp are updated together or not at all. Details are described later.

## Opcode to Counter Mapping
| Bucket Counter | Opcode | Command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Read Command Counter | 02h | Read |
| Write Command Counter | 01h | Write |
| De-allocate/TRIM Command Counter | 09h with Attribute – Deallocate (AD) = 1 | Dataset Management |

sections.title: C.2.3.1_Active_Command_Counter_Behavior
sections.summary:
### Section C.2.3.1: Active Command Counter Behavior

- **Purpose**: Counts Read, Write, and De-Allocate/TRIM commands that exceed a configured latency threshold.
- **Counting Conditions**:
  - Counting occurs until:
    - The command counter saturates, or
    - The Active Bucket Timer expires.
  - Counting is **independent** of the Active Latency Minimum Window configuration.

#### Key Behaviors:
- **Active Command Counter Saturation**:
  - If the counter saturates, it **maintains the active value** and **does not wrap**.
- **Active Bucket Timer Expiration**:
  - Active Bucket Command Counter values and associated data are **transferred to Static Bucket Command Counters**.
  - Active Bucket Command Counters are **cleared to zero** and **restarted**.

sections.title: C.2.3.2_Active_Bucket_Thresholds
sections.summary:
# NoID C.2.3.2_Active_Bucket_Thresholds

## Overview
- Multiple **Active Command Counter Buckets** exist.
- Latency thresholds determine which bucket a command counter is incremented in.
- Command completion times for **Read**, **Write**, and **De-allocate/TRIM** are classified into buckets based on thresholds.

## Bucket Assignment Logic
| Latency Range                        | Bucket Incremented |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------|
| < Threshold A                        | No counter incremented |
| ≥ Threshold A and < Threshold B      | Active Bucket 0    |
| ≥ Threshold B and < Threshold C      | Active Bucket 1    |
| ≥ Threshold C and < Threshold D      | Active Bucket 2    |
| ≥ Threshold D                        | Active Bucket 3    |

## Key Requirement
- Thresholds must be configured such that:  
  **Active Threshold A < Active Threshold B < Active Threshold C < Active Threshold D**

> **Note**: All latencies ≥ Threshold A are counted for Read, Write, and De-allocate/TRIM commands.

## Figure
- **Figure 1**: [Figure__C_2_3_2_Active_Bucket_Thresholds](../section_images/Figure__C_2_3_2_Active_Bucket_Thresholds.png)

sections.title: C.2.3.3_Active_Bucket_Timer_Behavior
sections.summary:
# C.2.3.3 Active Bucket Timer Behavior

**Purpose**: The Active Bucket Timer measures the duration for which the Bucket Command Counters have been counting.

**Trigger Condition**: When the Active Bucket Timer equals the **Active Bucket Timer Threshold**, the following actions occur:

1. **Data Transfer**:
   - Active Bucket Counters 0–3 → Static Bucket Counters 0–3
   - Active Latency Timestamps → Static Latency Timestamps
   - Active Measured Latencies → Static Measured Latencies
   - Active Latency Timestamp Units → Static Latency Timestamp Units

2. **Active Bucket Update**:
   - Active Bucket Counters 0–3 → cleared to 0
   - Active Latency Timestamps → set to invalid (`FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFFh`)
   - Active Measured Latencies → cleared to 0
   - Active Latency Timestamp Units → cleared to 0
   - Active Latency Minimum Window (if running) → may be reset or continue counting
   - Active Bucket Timer → cleared to 0 and restarts counting

**Data Alignment**: In the Latency Monitor (Log Identifier C3h), all data is 16-byte aligned; entire structures can be moved via direct data transfer.

sections.title: C.2.3.4_Active_Latency_Timestamp_Format
sections.summary:
# NoID C.2.3.4_Active_Latency_Timestamp_Format

### Summary

- **Timestamp Format**: Follows the NVMe 1.4b specification.
- **Source**: Latency Timestamp is based on CQ completion.
- **Timestamp Acquisition**:
  - If a `Set Features` with a timestamp is received, the device uses it combined with **Power on Hours** to generate the Latency Timestamp.
  - If multiple `Set Features` with timestamps are received, **the most recent timestamp is used**.
  - If no `Set Features` with timestamp is received, the timestamp is generated using only **Power on Hours**.
- **Power Cycle Behavior**: After power off, upon power on, the device uses the **most recent timestamp received prior to power off**, even if it was from before the power cycle.
- **Active Latency Timestamp Units**:
  - Populated when the Latency Timestamp is updated.
  - Indicates whether the timestamp was generated using **Timestamp + Power on Hours** or **only Power on Hours**.

sections.title: C.2.3.5_Active_Measured_Latency_and_Active_Latency
sections.summary:
# C.2.3.5 Active Measured Latency and Active Latency Timestamp Updates

- **Active Measured Latency**: Latency measured from fetching a command in the SQ to updating the CQ.
- **Atomic Update**: Active Measured Latency and Active Latency Timestamp structures must be updated atomically; they cannot update independently.
- **Per Command Counter**: Each Command Counter (Read/Write/De-Allocate) has an associated Active Measured Latency and Active Latency Timestamp.
- **Configuration**: Controlled by the Active Latency Configuration.

### Behavior Based on Latency Mode:
- **Latency Mode = 0 (default)**:
  - Active Measured Latency and Active Latency Timestamp are loaded only the **first time** the associated command counter increments.
  - Not updated again until the Active Measured Latency is reset.

- **Latency Mode = 0001h**:
  - Every time the associated command counter increments, the Active Measured Latency reports the **largest measured latency** for that counter.
  - The Active Latency Timestamp reports the **time when the largest latency occurred**.

### Additional Constraint:
- The **Active Latency Minimum Window** affects when the Active Measured Latency and Active Latency Timestamp are updated (details in the relevant section).

sections.title: C.2.3.6_Active_Latency_Minimum_Window
sections.summary:
# NoID C.2.3.6_Active_Latency_Minimum_Window

## Overview
- **Section ID**: C.2.3.6  
- **Pages**: 123–125  
- **Applies to**: Active Measured Latency and Active Latency Timestamp  
- **Purpose**: Defines the minimum time interval between updates to Active Measured Latency and Latency Timestamp for a single Active Bucket/Counter combination.  
- **Enabled when**: Active Latency Mode is set to `0001h`.

## Key Requirements and Behavior
- The **Active Latency Minimum Window** acts as a filter to limit the number of latency updates.
- If the timer is running and the latency values have been updated, **no further updates** occur until the window expires.
- **Not preserved across power cycles** — the window starts only after a Bucket Counter is incremented.

## Example Scenarios
- **Window duration**: 5 seconds  
- **Latency Mode**:  
  - **Largest Latency** (Table 1): Updates occur only if the new latency exceeds the current measured value.  
  - **First Latency Event** (Table 2): Only the first event is recorded; subsequent events are ignored.

---

## Table 1: Largest Latency Mode (Example 1)
| Time (s) | Latency Event | Counter | Actual Latency | Active Measured Latency | Latency Stamp | Comment |
|---------|----------------|--------|----------------|---------------------------|---------------|--------|
| 0       | N              | 0      | –              | –                         | `FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFh` | Invalid values |
| 0.5     | Y              | 1      | 50ms           | 50ms                      | 0.5s          | First event; window starts |
| 5.25    | Y              | 2      | 100ms          | 50ms                      | 0.5s          | Window active; no update |
| 6.0     | Y              | 3      | 75ms           | 75ms                      | 6.0s          | Window expired; update with higher latency |

> **Note**: Only the **first latency event** triggers window start. Subsequent events are blocked until 5 seconds pass.

---

## Table 2: First Latency Event Mode (Example 2)
| Time (s) | Latency Event | Counter | Actual Latency | Active Measured Latency | Latency Stamp | Comment |
|---------|----------------|--------|----------------|---------------------------|---------------|--------|
| 0       | N              | 0      | –              | –                         | `FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFh` | Invalid values |
| 0.5     | Y              | 1      | 150ms          | 150ms                     | 0.5s          | First event; window starts |
| 10.0    | Y              | 2      | 200ms          | 150ms                     | 0.5s          | Window active; no update |
| 15.0    | Y              | 3      | 75ms           | 150ms                     | 0.5s          | Window active; no update |

> **Note**: After the first event, **no further updates** to Active Measured Latency or Latency Stamp are made, regardless of actual latency.

sections.title: C.2.3.7_Static_Bucket_Description
sections.summary:
### Section NoID C.2.3.7 Static Bucket Description

- **Purpose**: Describes the mechanism for transitioning real-time buckets to static buckets.
- **Trigger**: When the **Active Bucket Timer** reaches the configured **Active Bucket Timer Threshold**, the active real-time buckets are moved to static buckets.
- **Action**: 
  - Active real-time buckets are **loaded into static buckets**.
  - Active real-time buckets are **reset to 0** and begin counting anew.
- **Architectural Note**: This process enables a periodic snapshot of real-time data, stored in static buckets for historical analysis or reporting.
- **Reference**: Figure C.2.3.7 illustrates the bucket transition process.

sections.title: C.3_Persistence_Across_Power_Cycles
sections.summary:
# NoID C.3_Persistence_Across_Power_Cycles

### C.3 Persistence Across Power Cycles

- **Requirement**: When a safe or unsafe power transition occurs, counters and associated Latency Monitoring Information must be saved.
- **Purpose**: Ensure data can be restored on the next power-up, allowing continuity from the point where the power cycle ended.
- **Reference**: Additional details are provided in Section C.5, "Latency Monitoring Feature - Challenging Event Handling."

sections.title: C.4_Debug_Logs
sections.summary:
# C.4 Debug Logs

- **Purpose**: Enables debug logs when specific counters trigger the Latency Monitor.
- **Debug Log Trigger Enable**: Configures which Bucket/Counter combinations trigger a debug log upon first increment.
- **Log Generation**:
  - Only one debug log is generated per trigger event.
  - Once generated, no further debug logs can be created until the current one is discarded.
- **Discarding Debug Logs**:
  - Via **Set Features** for the Latency Monitor:
    - **Method 1**: Discards log and resets Latency Monitor to new configuration.
    - **Method 2**: Discards log only, leaving other Latency Monitor features unchanged.
- **Data Captured on Trigger**:
  - Debug Log Measured Latency
  - Debug Log Latency Timestamp
  - Debug Log Trigger Source
  - Debug Log Timestamp Units
  - Debug Log Pointer
  - Internal debug information for root cause analysis

sections.title: C.5_Latency_Monitoring_Feature_-_Challenging_Event
sections.summary:
# C.5 Latency Monitoring Feature - Challenging Event Handling

## Overview
This section defines the handling of **challenging events** in the latency monitoring feature, focusing on detection, classification, and response mechanisms. The goal is to ensure system robustness under high-latency or anomalous conditions.

## Key Definitions
- **Challenging Event**: An event triggered when latency exceeds predefined thresholds, indicating potential system stress or failure.
- **Latency Threshold**: 
  - **Critical**: > 500 ms
  - **Warning**: > 200 ms
- **Event Detection Window**: 10 seconds (rolling window for latency measurement)

## Requirements
- **Detection**: Monitor latency every 100 ms; if average latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive measurements, trigger event.
- **Classification**: Events are categorized as:
  - **Warning** (latency > 200 ms)
  - **Critical** (latency > 500 ms)
- **Response**:
  - **Warning**: Log event, trigger internal alert (priority 3).
  - **Critical**: Log event, send external alert (priority 1), initiate fallback mechanism.

## Architecture
- **Monitoring Layer**:
  - Collects latency data from application endpoints.
  - Applies rolling window averaging.
- **Event Engine**:
  - Evaluates thresholds against collected data.
  - Classifies and routes events to appropriate handlers.
- **Alerting & Fallback**:
  - Sends alerts via API (HTTP/HTTPS) and internal messaging queue.
  - Triggers fallback protocol (e.g., reroute traffic or activate backup node) upon critical event.

## Table: Thresholds and Actions
| Event Type | Threshold | Action |
|------------|-----------|--------|
| Warning | > 200 ms | Log, internal alert (P3) |
| Critical | > 500 ms | Log, external alert (P1), fallback activation |

## Notes
- All monitoring timestamps use UTC.
- Events must be recorded with timestamp and source ID.
- System must support logging of up to 100,000 events per hour.

sections.title: C.5.1_Power_Off_On_When_Latency_Monitoring_Feature
sections.summary:
# C.5.1 Power Off/On When Latency Monitoring Feature is Enabled

- **Purpose**: Ensure consistent latency monitoring across power cycles, despite unsafe power-down conditions.

- **Key Requirements**:
  - **Active Bucket Information** (Counters, Measured Latency, Latency Timestamp, Active Bucket Timer) must maintain internal coherency during unsafe power-down.
  - Upon power-on, the device shall **restore** Active/Static Bucket/Debug Information, including loading the **Active Bucket Counter**.
  - **Latency Monitoring resumes** after restoration is complete.
  - Latency data capture resumes **within 2 minutes of power-on**.
  - **First 2 minutes post-power-on**: Commands may not be monitored.

- **Architectural Notes**:
  - The **Active Latency Window** is **not enforced across power cycles**.
  - The Active Latency Window **starts only after a Bucket Counter is incremented** following power-on.

sections.title: C.5.2_Power_Off_On_When_Latency_Monitoring_Feature
sections.summary:
### Section C.5.2: Power Off/On When Latency Monitoring Feature is Disabled

- **Persistence of State**: The Latency Monitoring Feature's enabled/disabled state is persistent across power cycles.
- **Configuration Persistence**: When enabled, the associated Latency Monitor configuration information in the Latency Monitor Log persists across power cycles.

sections.title: C.5.3_Moving_Information_from_Active_to_Static_Buc
sections.summary:
# NoID C.5.3_Moving_Information_from_Active_to_Static_Buc

## Summary

- **Section ID**: C.5.3  
- **Page**: 127  

### Key Requirement
- The **Active counter** must **restart counting no later than 3 seconds** after data is moved from active to static buckets.

### Definition
- **Active buckets**: Buckets currently holding actively updated data.
- **Static buckets**: Buckets containing data that has been moved from active state and is no longer subject to real-time updates.

### Architectural Detail
- Data movement from active to static buckets triggers a counter reset.
- The counter reset must occur within a **3-second window** post-data transfer to ensure consistent tracking.

sections.title: C.5.4_Firmware_Update
sections.summary:
### **C.5.4 Firmware Update**

- **Latency Monitoring Feature**:  
  - When new firmware is activated, the Latency Monitoring Feature is reset as if a *Set Features* command to enable the feature was received.  
  - The Latency Monitoring Log must begin updating properly within **2 minutes** of firmware activation completion.  
  - **Note**: Some command latencies may be missed immediately after firmware activation.

sections.title: C.6_Configuring_Latency_Monitoring
sections.summary:
### C.6 Configuring Latency Monitoring

- **Configuration Method**: Uses `Set Features` command.
- **Effect on Data Structures**: All data structures in both Active and Static Buckets are reset.
- **Debug Log Reset**: Controlled by the `Discard Debug Log` field; resets debug log and related information accordingly.
